newsitem.title: UK: Uganda set to win debt relief in March - UK's Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Uganda set to win debt relief in March - UK's Clarke.

text.p: Uganda is likely next month to become the first of several poor nations to benefit from an innovative scheme to reduce their debt to manageable levels, British Chancellor of Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday.

The scheme holds out the prospect of enhanced debt relief from the Paris Club of creditor nations, in tandem with a cut in debt owed to the IMF and World Bank, for countries that have successfully followed IMF-approved policies for three years.
Clarke told parliament's Treasury Committee that he had always considered Uganda to be a leading candidate to kick off the debt-relief programme.

"I hope that we'll have some decisions taken before the Spring meetings of the IMF and the World Bank and at the moment I hope we might get decisions taken on Uganda in March of this year," Clarke said.

He named Guyana, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast as other countries that stood to benefit from the scheme, which was agreed at last September's annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
"We are concentrating on the very poorest, good-performing countries which have established a sufficient track record... in order to get down the debt to a sustainable level," Clarke said.
A senior Treasury official, David Peretz, also named Mozambique and Nicaragua as likely to be among the early beneficiaries.
In addition to a decision on Uganda in March, Peretz told the committee: "I would hope that we can get decisions on three or four other countries over the course of the summer."
